title: Phased geo failover and residency-aware evacuation playbook for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines and implements a phased cross-region / multi-zone failover and evacuation playbook for Redwood Dedicated fleets that respects customer-configured data residency constraints while preserving throughput guarantees and minimizing customer-visible latency and errors. The goal is to provide deterministic, auditable behavior when a zone or region loses capacity (maintenance, cloud outage, network partition) and to expose safe controls for customers to specify residency constraints and acceptable fallback behavior.

Scope and motivation:
- Customers on Dedicated often require both throughput guarantees (reserved slices) and strong residency constraints (data must remain in a region or set of zones unless explicit allowlist says otherwise). Current evacuation behavior is all-or-nothing and can cause either opaque errors or sudden fail-open to non-compliant regions.
- We need a multi-stage evacuation that attempts local mitigation first, then controlled spillover into allowed candidates, and finally a graceful degradation path when no compliant capacity exists. Autoscaling policies must be coordinated with the playbook to avoid oscillation and to honor reserved throughput contracts.

High-level design decisions made so far:
1) Two-layer residency policy model: "Hard residency" (no cross-region fallback permitted) and "Soft residency" (fall back to an explicit secondary region with audit logging and customer opt-in). Customers can configure per-pool residency preferences in the Dedicated config API.
2) Phased evacuation windows: Pre-warning (T-30m) -> Soft-drain (T-10m) -> Hard-drain (immediate) with configurable grace periods per-customer. Soft-drain allows redirecting a bounded portion of traffic (e.g., 10-50%) to pre-warmed secondary pools while keeping the rest on the origin until capacity drops below a threshold.
3) Capacity hedging and prewarm: When a soft-residency allows a secondary region, we will pre-warm a small fleet (configurable % of committed throughput) using predictive warm-up before promoting traffic. Pre-warm has a cost budget and explicit customer opt-in by default (opt-out available).
4) Autoscale coordination: Autoscaler will expose a mode flag ("residency-aware") that postpones aggressive scale-to-zero and prefers gradual shrink with hedging. Scale-up in fallback region is rate-limited and paired with preference routing to avoid cascading short-lived replicas.
5) Routing & orchestration: Requests are routed by a placement controller that is residency-aware and will consult a policy engine before attempting cross-region placements. When no residency-compliant placement exists, the controller will return a deterministic error code with a remediation hint unless customer policy allows failover.

Acceptance criteria (see tasks below):
- Controlled phased evacuation can be triggered manually and by automated detectors (zone health signals) and completes without violating hard residency policies.
- Throughput guarantees (committed slices) are respected in origin or fallback region according to configured hedging; percent of throughput migration is observable in console.
- Autoscaling behavior under evacuation does not cause oscillation and respects committed capacity contracts.
- Audit trail is emitted for any cross-region traffic (region origin, failover reason, timestamps) and surfaced in console and logs.
- Playbook has runbook documentation and an SRE-run tabletop exercise completed before release.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1: API + schema updates for per-pool residency settings, grace windows, prewarm budget (backend + console flags). (Owner: PM / API eng)
- Week 2: Placement controller change: add residency policy check, deterministic error codes, and soft-drain fraction routing. (Owner: ENG)
- Week 3: Autoscaler changes: residency-aware mode, hedging support, ramp rate limits for cross-region scale-up. (Owner: ENG)
- Week 4: Prewarm orchestration: small prewarm fleet lifecycle + cost metering and opt-in flows. (Owner: ENG)
- Week 5: Observability & alerts: per-pool failover metrics, audit logs, console visualization, dashboard panels, and SLO recalculation rules. (Owner: Observability)
- Week 6: Runbook, tabletop, and staged rollout (canary customers then broader release). (Owner: SRE / PM)

Risks and trade-offs:
- Cost vs. availability: Prewarming secondary capacity increases cost; default conservative hedging and explicit opt-in mitigate surprise billing.
- Complexity in routing: Adding residency checks increases decision latency in the placement path; we will cache decisions and use a fast policy engine to keep p95 decision time under 5ms.
- Edge cases with mixed-customer tenancy: Some pooled GPUs host multiple tenants where per-tenant residency constraints differ; we will enforce tenancy isolation and consider creating residency-anchored pools for strict customers.

Docs and artifacts:
- PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/PRD-981234 (internal)
- Design sketch (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Phased+Geo+Failover (internal)
- Draft console mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folderview?id=mockups-981234
- Incident learnings referenced: PagerDuty Incident #INC-2025-11-zone-eject (summary attached)

Notes for reviewers:
- Evaluate whether the prewarm default should be opt-in or opt-out for customers with small committed slices. Current recommendation: opt-in with a single-click enable in console.
- Confirm the error codes and remediation hints are acceptable for SDKs and will be included in API docs.
- Performance budget: the placement controller must not add more than 5ms p95 latency to placement decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Phased evacuation executes without violating hard residency policies and logs all cross-region decisions
Committed throughput maintained within configured hedging % or appropriate deterministic errors are returned
Autoscale does not trigger oscillations during failover (observability tests pass under synthetic load)
Console surfaces failover audit trail and prewarm billing estimate
Runbook & SRE tabletop completed and documented
